# Engine-owned lock header action protects a dock pane

## Context

Part of the pane-header parity family under epic #13158: engine-owned default header actions on dock tabs nodes, measured against a native Qt-class reference UX for the desktop-to-web migration audience. `#17928` (maximize) is the intake-validated sibling. Family ordering contract (shared, frozen): **[tab overflow, only while overflowing] → [host actions] → [engine set: lock · reload · pin · pop-out · maximize — focus-gated] → [close — always visible, always last]**; `lock` carries ONE amendment to that gating, recorded 2026-08-31 and stated in full under *Reversibility exception* below; each engine action behind its own `enableDock<X>Action` boolean with the reserved-name guard extended. Anchors verified at Engine `dev@34499f737b`.

## The Problem

There is no way to protect a pane. Qt-class dock users lock a pane to mean two coupled things: **its content stops accepting interaction** (no accidental edits) and **the pane stops being structurally destructible** (no accidental close, drag-away, or tear-out). The dock has per-item *policy* fields that gate operations (`closable`, `pinnable` — both fail closed in the model), but no user-togglable protective state and no affordance to toggle one.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Per-item state precedent (shipped):** `pinned` / `autoHidden` are committed item fields with fail-closed operation guards (`src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs:368-408`); `closable: false` already makes `closeItem` fail closed (`Operations.mjs:340-346`). ADR 0029 §2.1 carries the committed-state amendments trail (`#17838`); §2.2 makes committed item state ride perspectives automatically.
- **Action substrate (shipped):** engine-action projection + reserved-name guard (`LayoutAdapter.mjs:958-1002`), Workspace dispatch (`Workspace.mjs:1250`), per-active-item `hidden` policy (`Workspace.mjs:1164`), `showOnFocus` gating (`toolbar/Base.mjs:255-301`).
- **Input-suppression precedent (frozen by `#17928`):** the Workspace already owns guarding its drag-source registration and key scopes on transient state; per-item guards extend the same pattern.

## The Fix

Two additive layers, following the `pinned`/`pinnable` shape exactly:

1. **Model:** committed item field `locked: false` + policy field `lockable` (absent = lockable), plus a NEW fail-closed operation `setItemLocked`. While `locked: true`, the destructive/structural operations on that item — `closeItem`, `detachItem`, `moveItem` (as source) — reject with a model error. Additive schema: documents without the field behave as `locked: false`.
2. **Workspace/action:** `enableDockLockAction: false`; on = a `lock` toggle at the frozen slot, focus-gated while UNLOCKED and persistent while LOCKED (see *Reversibility exception*) (icon pair, the `dialog.Base` toggle idiom `#17928` reuses). Locking the active pane: commit `setItemLocked(true)`; render the pane body inert; suppress the item's drag sources and hide its close action (per-active-item `hidden` sync — the policy mechanism `close` already uses for `closable: false`). Unlock reverses all of it.

**Body-disable mechanism (resolved at intake, engine-native):** the pane root's own **`vdom.inert`** surface — the idiom `toolbar.Base#applyContextualActionState` and `form.field.FileUpload#afterSetState` already ship for whole-subtree interaction exclusion. The Workspace resolves the live pane from the projected TabContainer, snapshots whether the root already OWNED `inert` (and its prior value) into a Workspace-owned `WeakMap` keyed by the pane, then sets `pane.vdom.inert = true` plus a stable `neo-dock-pane-locked` visual token in one update. Unlock restores the EXACT prior inert ownership/value — never a blind delete: a pane that was independently inert before the lock must remain inert after unlock. Works on arbitrary panes (no pane class implements anything), presentation-layer, reversible, no re-parenting.

**Drag-source mechanism (resolved at intake):** `draggable.container.DragZone` listens with the `.neo-draggable` delegate token, and the tab SortZone places that class on admitted tab buttons — so per-item source suppression is: map `dockItemIds` to the locked items' tab buttons and remove the class after projection/reconciliation; unlock/re-sync restores the SortZone-owned class. The model's `moveItem` guard stays the INDEPENDENT hard boundary beneath it (stale chrome or programmatic dispatch still rejects). Locked headers may remain drop TARGETS; the contract forbids moving the locked item as a SOURCE.

**Interplay (frozen here):** lock is orthogonal to rail state — a locked railed item still reveals (reading is not a mutation) but cannot be detached or moved; `#17928` maximize is presentation and stays allowed; in-strip reorder of a locked item's header is suppressed along with its cross-zone sources.

## Decision Record impact

`amends ADR 0029 §2.1` — one additive committed item field (`locked`) + its policy twin and state-table row; JSON-first guardrail satisfied (plain booleans, no runtime state persisted). The ADR amendment rides the implementing PR, the `#17838` precedent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Default off: byte-identical projection. On: a `lock` toggle at the frozen slot, reserved-name guard covering `lock` — focus-gated while the item is unlocked, persistent while it is locked.
- [ ] **Reversal reachability, witnessed with focus OUTSIDE the pane:** with the item locked and focus moved elsewhere, the `unlock` affordance is visible and actionable without first restoring focus to the pane. The sibling engine actions stay gated in that state — a locked pane offers its reversal, not its whole toolbar.
- [ ] Locking commits `setItemLocked(true)`; the pane body is inert (pointer + keyboard witnessed), the item's close action hides, and its drag sources (in-strip, cross-zone, tear-out) are suppressed — each witnessed.
- [ ] `closeItem` / `detachItem` / `moveItem` on a locked item fail closed at the model (witnessed as operation errors, headless).
- [ ] Unlock restores interaction, close visibility, and drag sources (each witnessed).
- [ ] A perspective round-trips `locked` (committed item state); documents predating the field load as `locked: false` (migration fixture).
- [ ] Falsifier — exact restore: a pane whose root is INDEPENDENTLY inert before locking goes through lock → unlock and remains inert (the WeakMap restore clause, witnessed).
- [ ] Falsifier — layered guards: with the presentation token removed (or the operation dispatched programmatically), `closeItem` / `detachItem` / source `moveItem` on the locked item still reject at the model (chrome is never the boundary).
- [ ] E2e gesture spec in the same PR (epic gesture-proof guardrail): lock → attempt close/drag → unlock → both succeed.

## Reversibility exception (amended 2026-08-31, on @neo-gpt's #17982 finding)

`lock` is focus-gated while the item is **unlocked**, and **persistent while it is locked**. The sibling engine actions stay gated throughout; a locked pane exposes its reversal, not its whole toolbar.

**The reason is affordance quality, not unreachability — and the difference matters, because the wrong reason would be frozen here for whoever reads this next.** @neo-gpt observed the action correctly gating to `context-inactive` once the pane was locked and focus left, and read that as the action making its own unlock unreachable. Measured against the shipped focus-gated siblings at `dev@fa20136f29`, it does not:

- the header toolbar and its tab buttons are **siblings** of `.neo-tab-body-container`, not descendants — rendered order is `[header toolbar, strip, body container]`
- setting `inert` on the pane root (this ticket's own lock mechanism) leaves `toolbar.inert === false` and `tabButton.inert === false`
- with the pane root inert and focus blurred away, `tabButton.focus()` **succeeds** — `document.activeElement` becomes the tab button
- and focusing a tab header demonstrably reveals the gated set: witnessed on the shipped `maximize` sibling in `apps/workstation`

So a locked pane's header stays focusable and the reversal is recoverable by clicking it. The amendment stands anyway, for the reason that survives the measurement: **a protective state that persists must not hide its own reversal behind a transient condition.** `close` is always visible because destruction must never be a surprise; `unlock` is persistent while locked for the mirror reason — a user who locked a pane, clicked away, and came back should see the way out rather than have to rediscover that focusing the header restores it. Discoverability, not reachability.

This is a per-state exception to the family's gating uniformity, and it is deliberate. It applies to `lock` alone because `lock` alone creates a persistent protective state; the other engine actions are momentary and their gating is unchanged.

## Out of Scope

- Permission/role semantics (who may unlock) — consumer policy on top of the state.
- Workspace-wide layout lock (a different, node-tree-level feature).
- Locking non-active items from the header (active-item grain, the `close` precedent).

### The body-inert mechanism

Use the component root’s native **`vdom.inert`** surface. This is already a shipped engine idiom:

- `toolbar.Base#applyContextualActionState` toggles `vdom.inert`, `aria-hidden`, and tab order; `TabHeaderActionsNL` witnesses focus/pointer exclusion and restoration.
- `form.field.FileUpload#afterSetState` uses the same native property for a whole interactive subtree.

For an arbitrary dock pane, Workspace can therefore:

1. resolve the live pane from the projected TabContainer;
2. snapshot whether its root already owned `inert` and the prior value in a Workspace-owned `WeakMap` keyed by the pane;
3. while locked, set `pane.vdom.inert = true`, add a stable `neo-dock-pane-locked` visual token, and update once;
4. on unlock, restore the exact prior inert ownership/value rather than blindly deleting it.

That restore clause is load-bearing: unlock must not make a pane interactive when the pane was independently inert before the lock.

### Drag-source mechanism

The registration boundary is also already explicit: `Neo.draggable.container.DragZone` listens with delegate `.neo-draggable`, and `adjustItemCls()`/the tab SortZone place that class on admitted tab buttons. Workspace can map `dockItemIds` to `getTabButtons()` and remove the class from every locked item after projection/reconciliation; unlock/re-sync restores the SortZone-owned class. The model’s `moveItem` guard remains the hard boundary for stale/programmatic dispatch. Locked headers may remain drop targets; the contract forbids moving the locked item as a source.

### Required body/ledger delta before claim

- Replace the body-inert “claim-time question” with the native inert + exact-restore contract above.

- Add a stale-chrome/model falsifier: remove the presentation token or dispatch programmatically; `closeItem` / `detachItem` / source `moveItem` must still reject.
